claim: As of 15 July 2026, Commerce had awarded CHIPS semiconductor incentives of approximately US$31.7 billion in direct funding to 24 companies for 49 projects (plus associated workforce activities).
evidence: "With these new awards, Commerce has awarded a total of 24 companies approximately $31.7 billion in direct funding for 49 projects (see fig. 1), as well as workforce activities associated with the projects." (GAO-26-109121, section "Commerce Awarded Nine Additional Projects Since July 2025")

metric.name: CHIPS incentive direct funding awarded (cumulative)
metric.population: Semiconductor incentive awards under FY21 NDAA s.9902, 24 companies, 49 projects, excl. Secure Enclave

notes: Adds USA Rare Earth, Bosch, Crucible Metals, Vulcan Elements and Powerex (9 projects) to the July 2025 set.

claim: As of 15 July 2026, Commerce had awarded a total of US$6.8 billion in CHIPS incentive loans to three companies.
evidence: "In addition, Commerce has now awarded a total of three companies $6.8 billion in loans." (GAO-26-109121, footnote 15)

metric.name: CHIPS incentive loans awarded (cumulative)
metric.population: Loans under CHIPS incentive awards (TSMC, SK hynix, USA Rare Earth)

notes: TSMC US$5.0bn + SK hynix US$0.5bn (GAO-26-107882 Table 2) + USA Rare Earth US$1.3bn (GAO-26-109121 Table 1).

claim: GAO reported that cumulative CHIPS incentive direct funding awards as of July 2026 represented approximately 89 percent of the US$35.5 billion available for the incentives program (excluding the US$3.5 billion Secure Enclave).
evidence: "This represents approximately 89 percent of the $35.5 billion available for the incentives program. [16]" Footnote 16: "The $35.5 billion in available funds does not include $3.5 billion appropriated for the Secure Enclave program." (GAO-26-109121)

metric.name: Share of available CHIPS incentive funds awarded
metric.population: Direct funding awarded vs US$35.5bn available (excl. Secure Enclave)

claim: As of April 2026, Commerce had disbursed US$13.1 billion of CHIPS incentive funding, about 42 percent of the US$31.2 billion in direct funding awards made by then.
evidence: "As of April 2026, Commerce disbursed $13.1 billion to awardees. This was approximately 42 percent of the total $31.2 billion in direct funding awards Commerce had made as of April 2026." (GAO-26-109121, section "Commerce Disbursed $13 Billion as of April 2026")

metric.name: CHIPS incentive funds disbursed
metric.population: Disbursements under CHIPS incentive awards, incl. Intel disbursements under its August 2025 amended agreement

notes: GAO's Highlights give the denominator as $31.5 billion; the body says $31.2 billion.

claim: GAO recommended in August 2026 that Commerce's CHIPS R&D Office (1) develop a plan and timeline for how the National Semiconductor Technology Center will meet FY21 NDAA requirements, (2) either decide promptly on the two existing NAPMP awards or plan how to meet NAPMP requirements, and (3) plan and time the re-establishment of the Industrial Advisory Committee; Commerce agreed.
evidence: "develops a plan and timeline with sufficient detail to address how and when the National Semiconductor Technology Center will align with all applicable requirements in the FY21 NDAA. (Recommendation 1)"; "fully implements the NAPMP requirements by either (a) making a timely decision to move forward with the two existing awards or (b) developing a plan and timeline ... (Recommendation 2)"; "develops a plan and timeline describing how and when Commerce will reestablish the Industrial Advisory Committee ... (Recommendation 3)"; "Commerce agreed with the recommendations." (GAO-26-109121)

claim: Wolfspeed's section 48D cash refunds received (US$186.5 million in fiscal 2025 plus US$698.6 million in December 2025, about US$885 million) exceed the US$750 million CHIPS grant it was offered but never finalised, so for Wolfspeed the tax credit delivered more cash than the grant programme.
evidence: Arithmetic from CLM-1008 ("received $698.6 million"; "In fiscal 2025, the Company received $186.5 million") and CLM-0933 (Wolfspeed US$750m preliminary terms still not finalised as of 10 June 2026).
notes: Inference from CLM-1008 and CLM-0933. US$698.6m alone is below US$750m.

claim: The Motley Fool reported that Wolfspeed's shares fell nearly in half on 28 March 2025 after rumours that the company would not receive the US$750 million in CHIPS Act funding agreed under the prior administration.
evidence: "the very next day, Wolfspeed's stock plunged nearly in half, accounting for pretty much the entire month's losses ... That morning, rumors began circulating that the company would not receive the $750 million in CHIPS Act funding that the government had agreed to pay Wolfspeed during the prior administration." (Motley Fool, 7 Apr 2025)
notes: Drops the unsupported 'largest proposal not finalised' part of CLM-1010.
